mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 1% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of months following a 1%+ INDPRO drop, indicating that the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, increasing by more than 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period, signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises and retail sales remain strong during periods of rising unemployment, indicating that the labor market weakness is not impacting consumer behavior.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Equity market volatility, as measured by the VIX, remains low (< 20) despite high real rates, indicating that investors are not overly concerned about the restrictive monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Homebuilder stocks outperform the broader market despite the drop in housing starts, indicating that investors expect a quick recovery in the housing market.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM manufacturing PMI falls below 45, it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face reduced demand and lower profits.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of the 20-day periods following an ISM_MFG reading below 45, indicating that the market is not concerned about the manufacturing contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the yield curve inverts (10-year yield falls below the 2-year yield), it signals a coming recession that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors reassess risk and move away from equities.
failure_condition: Equity market volatility remains low and credit spreads do not widen significantly following the yield curve inversion, indicating that investors do not expect a severe recession.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales decline for two consecutive months, it signals weakening consumer demand that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face lower revenues and profits.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises and other measures of consumer spending (e.g., credit card spending) remain strong despite the drop in retail sales, indicating that the weakness is likely temporary.
